html:
The Olmecs were the first major civilisation of Mesoamerica, based in the swampy lowlands of Mexico's Gulf coast (modern Veracruz and Tabasco) from about 1200 BCE to about 400 BCE.

Their story is told by their centres, which rose and fell one after another:

  • San Lorenzo was the first great centre, until about 900 BCE.
  • La Venta then took its place, with a large earthen pyramid and buried offerings of jade.
  • By about 400 BCE the major centres had been abandoned and the population of the heartland fell sharply. There was no single dated collapse.

The Olmecs are best known for their art, above all the colossal stone heads, carved from basalt hauled many kilometres. They also seem to have started habits that nearly every later Mesoamerican society shared: ritual bloodletting, the rubber ball game (see rubber and the ballgame), and a shared set of gods and symbols.

That is why they are sometimes called the "mother culture" of Mesoamerica, though many scholars now prefer to see them as one strong voice among several neighbours. Their style faded, but its elements lived on in the Maya, the Zapotecs and others. We do not know what the Olmecs called themselves; "Olmec" is an Aztec word meaning "rubber people".
sum: The Olmecs were the first major civilisation of Mesoamerica, based in the swampy lowlands of Mexico's Gulf coast (modern Veracruz and Tabasco) from about 1200 BCE to about 400 BCE.
